verdicts.note: The cached Priorities page has 'living within our budgetary means and making every dollar count' alongside calls to increase state investment in housing [S3]. A 0 for a genuinely mixed position is correct, not a placeholder for unknown.

The same bullet list on the cached Priorities page pairs 'Increase state investments in affordable housing development' with 'Reduce unnecessary permitting delays and regulatory barriers' [S3]. Both poles are present, so 0 is correct.

'Public safety requires both immediate response and long-term prevention,' with staffing and prevention planks side by side [S3]. Her no vote on the Vancouver police sales tax was about the tax, not the spending; she said she supports public-safety investment [S8]. It does not move this axis.

She has no legislative tenure but a sitting councilorship since 2022 and two state commission seats [S1][S4], and she runs against a first-term incumbent. Neither the proven-record pole nor the outsider pole fits well, so 0 is defensible.

The lone-ESSB-6346 rule does not bind here. Besides the 6346 no vote [S3], the dossier has three independent recorded no votes on 2025 revenue bills (verified in the cached roll calls) [S5][S6][S7]. It also has his sponsored amendment 2564, whose EFFECT clause cuts the state sales tax from 6.5% to 5% effective July 1, 2028 [S4], and an explicit op-ed plank, verified in the cache, for 'no new taxes' and a two-thirds vote to raise them [S15]. Any one of these is enough for -2/high.

Verified in the cached op-ed: 'we have a spending problem' and tying budget growth to inflation and population [S15]. Also verified: his call to eliminate programs without a return on investment [S16] and two no votes on the operating budget [S8]. A record plus repeated explicit statements supports -2/high.

The S16 items (blocking shorter sentences for serious crimes and blocking limits on local camping-law enforcement) are framed as House Republican caucus accomplishments, not as his own bills. Medium is the right level.

The axis applies to State contests. Restoring the $782M Medicaid cut, repealing 'artificial pricing policies' and supporting rural hospitals [S15], plus HB 2531 on ambulance Medicaid funding [S16], all work within the existing system. That is pole_a, and nothing points toward single-payer.
He voted no on ESHB 1296 House passage and concurrence [S11], and the bill revised the I-2081 parental rights [S12]. That is one bill with no I-1 statement, so -1/medium.

missing.basis: Cast the lone council vote against Vancouver's 0.1% public-safety sales tax, citing 'the cumulative tax burden that continues to be placed on all of us' and its effect on lower-income residents. Her objection centers on a regressive local tax and on timing, and she states no position on state progressive revenue, so the direction on this axis is uncertain and only low confidence is warranted.
